# Country messaging rules

Generated by `scripts/generate-ai-reference.ts` from `server/services/compliance/country-rules.ts`, `server/services/compliance/quiet-hours.ts`.
Do not edit this file by hand. Run `npm run generate:ai-reference` after changing the
source, and `npm run verify:ai-reference` to prove it is still true.

## Quiet hours are per country, not global

Sendly holds rules for **205 countries**. 189 of them use 21:00 to 08:00 in the recipient's local time, the US federal TCPA window. **16 do not.**

If you hard code the US window into your own scheduler you will hold back sends that are legal,
and worse, release sends that are not. Ask Sendly instead of reimplementing this: send with
`messageType: "marketing"` and the send is checked against the recipient's own country before it
goes out.

### Transactional messages are exempt

`checkQuietHours()` returns `allowed` immediately when `messageType` is `transactional`, whatever
the country and whatever the hour. Alerts, receipts and one-time passcodes are transactional.
Anything promotional is `marketing` and is subject to the table above. Choosing the label
correctly is your obligation, not a switch to get around quiet hours.

### Countries with no entry

An unrecognised country falls back to `CONSERVATIVE_DEFAULT`: 20:00 to 09:00, no Sunday.
A number that cannot be parsed at all is blocked outright rather than allowed through.

### Consent

Every one of the 205 countries requires **explicit** consent.
There is no jurisdiction in the table where an unsolicited marketing message is acceptable.
